`abstract class IntegerSliderNode`<br/>
**Extends:** [`SliderNode<Integer>`](/reference/controls/slidernode/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.node.impl.control.slider` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IntegerSliderNode.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/node/impl/control/slider/IntegerSliderNode.java)

A slider over a range of integers.

![A slider whose thumb sits at 4 of 10; the pointer drags the thumb to the end of the track, to its start, then back to 4](/captures/catalog-controls-integerslidernode.webp)

## Description

A skin extends it and gives its parts as for any [`SliderNode`](/reference/controls/slidernode/).

## Creation details

<a id="IntegerSliderNode-constructor"></a>

### IntegerSliderNode

`IntegerSliderNode(double x, double y, double width, double height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Creates the slider at `x`, `y` with a `width` and a `height` in design pixels, from the constructor of a skin.

## Method details

<a id="IntegerSliderNode-method-range"></a>

### range

`this range(int min, int max)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Gives the options every integer from `min` to `max`, both included.
Throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when `min` is above `max`, or when the range holds more values than `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, as `range(0, Integer.MAX_VALUE)` does.

`this range(int min, int max, int step)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalArgumentException`: The step … of the slider range must be positive, pass a step of 1 or more
- `IllegalArgumentException`: The min … of the slider range is above its max …, pass a min of at most …
- `IllegalArgumentException`: The slider range from … to … by … holds more than … values, pass a narrower range or a larger step

Gives the options from `min` to `max` by `step`; `max` is an option only when a step lands on it.
Throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the step is not positive, when `min` is above `max`, or when the range holds more values than `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.
The options are computed on demand, so a large range costs nothing.

<a id="IntegerSliderNode-method-fallback"></a>

### fallback

`Integer fallback(Integer value)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Returns the option nearest to the value asked for, the smaller one on a tie, whatever the order of the options.

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
